plan.title: Liver QuantSeq 3' treated vs control DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000 x 6 raw integer gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column, one column per sample) from STAR/featureCounts on a Lexogen QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq run of human liver, with metadata.csv giving one condition label per sample: 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. The research question is purely 'which genes differ between treated and control', so the plan stops at the differential expression result and its report — no enrichment step is added, because none was asked for.

Three facts of this dataset drive the method choices. First, the library is 3' tag-seq: one read per transcript molecule at the 3' end, with no dependence on transcript length. The counts therefore go into the model as raw integers with no length correction, no tximport, and no length-normalized unit (TPM/FPKM does not apply here); the low-count pre-filter also uses a lower floor (5 counts in at least 3 samples, the smallest group size) than the usual full-length default of 10, because a long gene collects proportionally fewer reads in a 3' library. Second, the counts come from an aligner plus a counter, so no bias model ran at quantification — a GC-content diagnostic is drawn (GC only, not length, since a 3' count carries no length term); cqn and EDASeq, the tools of record for correcting such a trend, are absent from this environment, so a detected trend is reported as a caveat and a request, not silently corrected. Third, three replicates per group is a low-power design: both count models recover only a minority of true differential genes, mostly those with large fold changes. The plan states the expected power up front, keeps alpha at 0.05, and never loosens the threshold to compensate.

T1S1 does the sample-structure QC on blind VST (PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) before any test, so an outlier or a failed sample is visible before the model. T1S2 fits DESeq2 with ~condition, control set as the explicit reference so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated, runs the Wald test, shrinks the reported fold change with apeglm, and applies BH with independent filtering at alpha 0.05; the p-value histogram is inspected before the adjustment is trusted. T1S3 runs edgeR quasi-likelihood with TMM on the same filtered counts as an independent second method; the intersection of the two significant sets is the high-confidence result, and method-unique genes are reported as a secondary set rather than a union. T1S4 assembles the report with the MA and dispersion plots, both shrunken and unshrunken effect sizes, the outlier-NA and filter-NA counts kept apart, the power statement, and the full reproducibility record.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Low count filter for a 3' tag library: at least 5 counts in at least 3 samples
Median-of-ratios size factors inside DESeq2, with a GC-content bias diagnostic (no length plot, 3' library)
~ condition with control as explicit reference level, raw integer counts, no length correction, expected-power statement
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the robustness second method
DE report: MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, shrunken and unshrunken LFC, method overlap, power statement, sessionInfo

steps.context: The research question asks only which genes differ — no enrichment or pathway step was requested, so none is included. The report is the deliverable, and its job is to make the low-power limit of a 3-vs-3 design explicit rather than to present a long gene list as if it were complete.
acceptance_criteria: The report names the method, package versions, design formula, contrast direction, thresholds, number of genes tested after filtering, and number of DE genes, all before the gene tables
An MA plot (on the shrunken fold changes, significant genes marked) and a dispersion plot are included, each with a one-line statement of what it shows
The p-value histogram and the GC-content diagnostic from T1S2 are included with their interpretation
The gene table carries baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue, padj, and the edgeR agreement flag; genes are ranked by the shrunken value

A power statement appears explicitly: at 3 replicates per group both count models recover a minority of true differential genes, mostly large-fold-change ones, so absence from the list is not evidence of no change
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, the seed, and package versions is stored with the results, not in a separate note
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit
Report both shrunken and unshrunken effect sizes — never the shrunken value alone and never a ranking on the unshrunken value alone
Report the intersection of DESeq2 and edgeR as the high-confidence set; do not present the union
Do not add enrichment, pathway, or gene-set analysis — it was not asked for
Keep alpha at 0.05 in the report; do not present a second, looser threshold as an alternative result
caveats: With 6 samples total and 12,000 genes, the significant list may be short or empty. An empty or short list is a legitimate result of a low-power design and must be reported as such, not rescued by loosening the threshold.
Gene symbols are the only identifier in counts.csv; symbols are not stable across annotation releases, so state the fact that no Ensembl or Entrez key is available for these rows.

grounding.reason: Report content set by R-0041 (method, versions, design, thresholds, counts), R-0087 (MA and dispersion plots), R-0085 (shrunken and unshrunken effect columns, rank on shrunken), R-0094 (power statement at 3 replicates), R-0042 (method overlap) and R-0086 (reproducibility record).
